title: Fiscal Balance, Trade Openness, and GDP in SAARC Countries (2000–2024)
text: Summary Fiscal balance, trade openness, and GDP vary significantly across SAARC countries over the past two decades. This project explores how fiscal policy and trade patterns relate to economic output in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka from 2000 to 2024. Using data from the World Bank’s WDI API, I cleaned and analyzed three key indicators: GDP, fiscal balance, and trade as % of GDP. The main plot reveals a strong positive association between trade openness and GDP levels, particularly in more integrated economies like India and Bangladesh.

title: Source
text:
The data for this project comes from the World Bank’s World Development Indicators (WDI), accessed using the WDI R package. I selected three variables: GDP in current US dollars (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD), fiscal balance as a % of GDP (GC.BAL.CASH.GD.ZS), and trade as % of GDP (NE.TRD.GNFS.ZS).
Data was retrieved for SAARC member countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, for the years 2000 to 2024.
Cleaning steps included renaming variables, filtering missing values, and excluding observations where any of the three main indicators were NA.
